title: session_store.record_event() loses writes under real concurrent multi-process access (inode-orphaning race in _maybe_compact())
claim_affected: Session/interaction history recorded via record_event() is durable and complete for a given session_id.
evidence: test_session_store_concurrency.py: 6 real OS processes x 200 unique-content writes each = 1200 total writes to the same session_id, production compaction thresholds left at default (_MAX_RECORDS=300, _COMPACT_TO=150) so multiple organic compaction cycles occur mid-run.

Fresh run this segment, hermetic HOME=/var/folders/.../chuzom-audit-c-home-n4k25glc: 22/1200 (1.83%) writes lost -- e.g. proc 1 lost 5/200 at seqs [113,142,168,169,197], proc 2 lost 5/200 at seqs [51,78,105,154,155].
final_line_count=253 corrupt_lines=0 -- every surviving line is well-formed JSON, ruling out torn/interleaved writes as the mechanism.

record_event() calls _maybe_compact() inline after every append; compaction rewrites to a tempfile and os.replace()s it over the session path, with no explicit lock (file lock, asyncio.Lock, or OS advisory lock) coordinating concurrent writers against that replace.
Losses are silent: record_event() raised no exception to any of the 22 lost calls; loss was only detected by the test harness's independent post-write readback of the file.
reproduction: Observe per-process LOST counts and final RESULT: FAIL when total_lost_via_readback > 0.
expected: All 1200 record_event() calls across 6 concurrent processes are present in the final session file, or a call that will not persist raises an exception to its caller.
actual: 22/1200 calls (1.83%) returned normally (no exception) but are absent from the final file; 0 corrupt lines, consistent with an inode-orphaning race between a writer's open file handle and a concurrent os.replace() during compaction.
impact: Any deployment where multiple processes/agents can append to the same session_id concurrently (e.g. multiple MCP server workers, multi-agent fan-out sharing a session) will silently lose a small but consistent fraction of recorded events, with no error surfaced to callers and no way to detect the loss after the fact short of independent auditing.
root_cause: record_event() appends without holding any lock around the read-modify-compact-replace cycle in _maybe_compact(); a writer that has an open handle/fd against the pre-compaction file (or that resolves the path just before a concurrent os.replace() swaps the inode) can have its write land on an orphaned inode that is no longer reachable via the session's canonical path.
recommended_fix: Serialize record_event()/_maybe_compact() per session_id with an OS-level advisory lock (e.g. fcntl.flock on a sidecar lock file) or a single-writer queue/actor per session_id; alternatively, switch the session store to an append-only, lock-free-safe backend (e.g. SQLite WAL, as already used successfully by budget_backend.py) instead of tempfile+os.replace() JSONL compaction under concurrent writers.
regression_test: Extend test_session_store_concurrency.py (or port it into the project's pytest suite) to run as a marked slow/integration test: N processes x M unique writes to one session_id, assert total_lost_via_readback == 0 and corrupt_lines == 0 after the run, with production _MAX_RECORDS/_COMPACT_TO thresholds so compaction fires organically during the test.

title: model_override is silently overridden by the process-global quality-feedback circuit breaker once a model's rolling quality average degrades
confidence: HIGH (source-confirmed root cause + execution-confirmed at soak scale + exact quantitative cross-validation)
claim_affected: Passing model_override to route_and_call() guarantees that exact model is used ('If set, use only this model' per _build_and_filter_chain's own docstring).
evidence: soak_driver.py: 5418 sequential route_and_call() calls with model_override='openai/gpt-4o-mini' against a monkeypatched _call_text. First 3 iterations dispatch to openai/gpt-4o-mini as requested; starting at iteration 4, 5415/5418 (99.94%) instead log 'Skipping low-quality model for generate/moderate: openai/gpt-4o-mini' -> 'Primary balanced chain exhausted, attempting BUDGET emergency fallback' -> fallback_model=ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b, with no exception raised.

src/chuzom/router.py _build_and_filter_chain(), docstring line 342: 'model_override: If set, use only this model (with subscription validation).' Implementation, line 387: 'return [model_override]' -- a single-element candidate chain.

src/chuzom/router.py lines 1993-2003 (per-model dispatch loop): unconditional call to quality_feedback.should_skip_model(model, task_type.value, c.value); if True, logs 'model_quality_skip' and `continue`s -- applied identically whether models_to_try came from a dynamic multi-model chain or a single-element model_override chain; no bypass/exemption exists for the override case.

src/chuzom/quality_feedback.py: _quality_store is a process-global, in-memory dict keyed by (model, task_type, complexity) with no session/caller scoping (line ~81); _MIN_CALLS_FOR_SIGNAL=3 (line ~84) and QUALITY_THRESHOLD=0.4 (line ~87) exactly match the soak observation (skip begins at the 4th call); should_skip_model() returns True once call_count>=3 and avg_quality<0.4.

Hand-verified score_response() rubric against the soak's exact fake content for task_type='generate': 0.1 (non-empty) + 0.2 (no refusal phrases) with no length/structure/punctuation bonus = 0.3 exactly, matching the soak log's observed avg=0.3 and confirming the mechanism is deterministic and fully characterized, not merely correlated.
reproduction: Cross-check source: grep -n 'return \[model_override\]' src/chuzom/router.py; sed -n '1985,2005p' src/chuzom/router.py; sed -n '1,100p' src/chuzom/quality_feedback.py
expected: route_and_call(..., model_override='openai/gpt-4o-mini') dispatches to openai/gpt-4o-mini for every call, or raises/signals clearly to the caller if it cannot (e.g. subscription-mode block, which router.py DOES already handle explicitly with a logged warning and explicit fallback-chain substitution).
actual: After 3 calls to a given (model, task_type, complexity) triple score an average quality below 0.4, every subsequent call using model_override for that exact triple is silently redirected to a different model/provider (observed: ollama/qwen2.5-coder:7b) for the remaining lifetime of the process, with resp.model/resp.provider reflecting the substitute and no caller-visible error, warning, or flag.
impact: Breaks the documented 'use only this model' contract for model_override. Any caller relying on explicit model selection for reproducibility, cost control, provider-compliance routing, or A/B/benchmark comparison gets silently wrong results. Because _quality_store is process-global and unscoped by caller/session/agent, one caller's poor-quality traffic for a given (model, task_type, complexity) can silently redirect ALL other callers in the same long-lived process (e.g. a shared MCP server) who explicitly request that exact model for that same task_type/complexity -- a cross-caller isolation violation, not just a single-session quirk.
root_cause: The per-model quality-feedback skip check in the router's dispatch loop is applied unconditionally to every candidate in models_to_try, including the single-element list produced when model_override is set, with no code path exempting an explicit override from the quality gate.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit bypass: when the current model came from model_override (not a dynamically-built fallback chain), skip the should_skip_model() gate entirely, OR raise a clear, typed exception (e.g. ModelQualityDegradedError) to the caller instead of silently substituting, so the caller can decide whether to accept the fallback. Additionally, scope _quality_store per-session/per-caller (or at minimum expose an opt-out flag on route_and_call, e.g. respect_override_strictly=True) to eliminate the cross-caller poisoning vector.
regression_test: Unit test: seed quality_feedback._quality_store with 3+ low-quality (<0.4) records for (model='x', task_type='generate', complexity='moderate'); call route_and_call(..., model_override='x', ...) and assert resp.model == 'x' (not silently substituted), or assert a typed exception/flag is raised instead of a silent substitution.

title: Router's output-length gate rejects short responses and silently double-dispatches via 'BUDGET emergency fallback' with no caller-visible signal
confidence: MEDIUM (source-class-confirmed; directly observed only in test-harness iteration, not independently reproduced against production traffic this segment)
component: src/chuzom/router.py (post-dispatch response-length gate, shared 'BUDGET emergency fallback' path also used by CHZ-AUD-C-02)
claim_affected: A single route_and_call() invocation results in at most one underlying model dispatch per attempted model in its chain, and any response substitution is either an explicit error or clearly attributable in the response.
evidence: soak_driver.py docstring (lines 12-17), itself written from a direct empirical observation while developing the soak harness: the first run of soak_smoke.py, before its fake response content was lengthened to pass the router's minimum output-length check, produced 10 _call_text invocations for 5 iterations (a 2x ratio) -- i.e. a response shorter than the length floor is rejected post-dispatch and triggers a second, silent dispatch via the same 'BUDGET emergency fallback' path used by CHZ-AUD-C-02, without raising to the caller.

soak_smoke.py's fake_call_text was subsequently fixed to return a >=20-char content string specifically to avoid this gate, and the corrected version produces exactly 1 invocation per iteration (confirmed both in soak_smoke.py's 5-iteration run and soak_driver.py's 5418-iteration full soak: fake_call_text_invocations=5418 == N exactly).
reproduction: Not independently re-executed against a fresh short-content fake this segment (the finding is preserved from the harness-development record rather than freshly re-run). To reproduce: revert soak_smoke.py's fake_call_text content to a string under the router's length floor and re-run; compare _call_count to iteration count.
expected: A single route_and_call() invocation results in exactly one dispatch per model actually needed, and any automatic quality-driven re-dispatch is either surfaced to the caller or at minimum distinguishable via response metadata.
actual: A response shorter than the router's minimum output-length floor triggers a second, silent dispatch through the same emergency-fallback mechanism used by the quality-feedback skip (CHZ-AUD-C-02), invisible to the caller beyond the final substituted response.
impact: Same class of caller-invisible substitution as CHZ-AUD-C-02, triggered by a different gate (raw response length rather than rolling quality average); also means short-but-correct responses (e.g. 'OK', a valid single-word answer) can trigger an unnecessary second, slower/costlier dispatch -- a concern independently flagged in the router's own source comments near the escalation logic ('escalating a short-but-correct answer... into a slow reasoning model').
root_cause: The output-length gate and the quality-feedback skip both funnel into the same undifferentiated 'BUDGET emergency fallback' path with no caller-visible distinction between 'the requested model failed/was unavailable' and 'the requested model succeeded but was judged too short/low-quality after the fact.'
recommended_fix: Surface which gate triggered a fallback (length vs. quality vs. availability) in response metadata or structured logs at a level the caller can act on; consider allow-listing legitimately short valid responses (e.g. yes/no, single-token) via a task-type-aware minimum-length threshold rather than a fixed floor.
regression_test: Unit test: monkeypatch _call_text to return a response just under the length floor for a task_type where short answers are valid (e.g. a yes/no classification task); assert the router either accepts it without a second dispatch, or clearly flags the substitution to the caller.

title: chuzom verify's hook health check covers only 3 of the 13 hooks actually installed by install_hooks.py
claim_affected: `chuzom verify` accurately reports the health of the installed hook set (especially meaningful now that CHZ-PKG-005's exit-code propagation fix makes verify's pass/fail result load-bearing for CI/install gates).
evidence: src/chuzom/commands/verify.py lines 158-183: check_hooks() hardcodes hook_names = ['chuzom-auto-route.py', 'chuzom-session-end.py', 'chuzom-enforce-route.py'] -- exactly 3 entries.

src/chuzom/install_hooks.py, hook manifest tuples around lines 309-350: install at least 13 distinct hooks, including chuzom-session-start.py, chuzom-status-bar.py (and/or chuzom-status-bar-clawcode.py), chuzom-agent-route.py, chuzom-subagent-start.py, chuzom-usage-refresh.py, chuzom-cc-usage-track.py, chuzom-agent-depth-release.py, chuzom-playwright-compress.py, chuzom-bash-compress.py, chuzom-context-capture.py, in addition to the 3 that verify.py does check.

10 of the 13 installed hooks (session-start, status-bar, agent-route, subagent-start, usage-refresh, cc-usage-track, agent-depth-release, playwright-compress, bash-compress, context-capture) are never checked by check_hooks() at all -- a missing, corrupted, or non-executable copy of any of these 10 is invisible to `chuzom verify`, silent or not.
expected: chuzom verify's hook check enumerates (or otherwise validates coverage against) the same set of hooks that install_hooks.py actually installs.
actual: check_hooks() checks a fixed list of 3 hook filenames, a strict subset of the 13 the installer deploys; 10 installed hooks have no corresponding health check.
impact: Now that CHZ-PKG-005 (verify's exit-code discard) is fixed and `chuzom verify`'s exit code is meaningfully used by CI/install gates, a correct exit code is only as trustworthy as the completeness of the checks behind it -- a broken/missing install of ~77% of the actually-installed hooks (10/13) would still report a clean/passing verify result.
root_cause: check_hooks()'s hook_names list was hardcoded at some point and not kept in sync with install_hooks.py's manifest as new hooks were added.
recommended_fix: Derive check_hooks()'s expected hook list from the same source of truth as install_hooks.py (e.g. a shared constant/manifest) instead of a separately hardcoded literal, so new hooks are automatically covered by verify.
regression_test: Add a test asserting set(verify.check_hooks.__globals__['hook_names']) (or the refactored equivalent) is a superset of every hook filename referenced in install_hooks.py's install manifests, failing the build if a new hook is added to the installer without a corresponding verify check.

title: IDE workspace-config writers (mcp.json, KIMI.md, .github) resolve paths via Path.cwd(), risking writes into the real Chuzom repo checkout
claim_affected: chuzom install/setup writes IDE integration files only into the intended target project, not into whatever directory the command happens to be run from.
evidence: grep -n 'Path.cwd()' src/chuzom/cli.py (fresh this segment): line 233 (.vscode/mcp.json), line 245 (.github), line 406 (.windsurf/mcp.json), line 418 (.github), line 463 (.kimi/mcp.json), line 475 (KIMI.md) -- six distinct writers all resolving relative to the process's current working directory rather than an explicit target-path argument.
reproduction: (Not executed against the real repo to avoid mutating it, per hermeticity constraints -- the risk is demonstrated by direct source inspection, not by reproducing the mutation.)
expected: IDE workspace-config writers operate against an explicitly specified or safely-detected target project directory, independent of the invoking shell's current working directory.
actual: All six writers use Path.cwd() directly; running an install/setup subcommand while cd'd into the actual Chuzom repo checkout (a realistic scenario for a Chuzom contributor, or any user who cd's into a git repo before installing) will read/write .vscode/mcp.json, .windsurf/mcp.json, .kimi/mcp.json, .github/, and KIMI.md inside that real repo/project rather than a sandboxed or explicitly-chosen location.
impact: A developer working inside the Chuzom repo itself (or any other git checkout) who runs an install/setup command without first cd'ing elsewhere risks unintended, uncommitted modifications to real project files -- low severity because it requires the operator to be inside a specific directory at invocation time, but the failure mode (silent file writes into version-controlled project files) is the kind of thing that produces confusing diffs and accidental commits.
root_cause: Path.cwd() is used directly at each of the 6 call sites instead of threading through an explicit target-directory parameter validated/confirmed against user intent.
recommended_fix: Require an explicit --target/--project-dir argument (or interactively confirm the resolved cwd-based path with the user before writing) for all workspace-config-writing subcommands; consider warning/refusing when cwd itself looks like the Chuzom project's own source checkout.
regression_test: Test that invoking the relevant install/setup subcommand with cwd pointed at a throwaway tmp dir writes files only under that tmp dir, and add an assertion/guard test that cwd resolution is never silently used when a target path is available from configuration or arguments.
